doom.driver: War between U.S. and Iran becomes a test of who will blink first. More than six months into the conflict between the U.S. and Iran, it's become a high-stakes game of endurance.
doom.summary: The US-Iran war has officially entered 'game of chicken played by people who hate each other' territory, with Iran dangling Strait of Hormuz reopening as a diplomatic carrot while its Houthi proxies push deeper into Yemen and displace 100,000 people. Meanwhile Trump is heading to UNGA to 'look for wins after a rough week,' which is not exactly the energy you want from the guy holding the nuclear codes. The F-35 parts disappearing in Hong Kong are doing their own quiet geopolitical thriller subplot in the background.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Six-month US-Iran conflict now a war of attrition, Houthis expanding territory, Strait of Hormuz leverage being played, and South China Sea collision between China and Philippines all running simultaneously.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Trump launches 'Trump TV' after banning CNN, MSNBC and Politico from White House, while UN General Assembly convenes with US war crimes allegations on the agenda.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Meta's Muse AI agent has a serious zero-day exploit patched same week as 2.5M downloads surge, and autonomous weapons top the UNGA agenda.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: MIT Tech Review pushes back on AI hype cycle, while OpenAI solved Navier-Stokes but mathematicians say they learned nothing from how it did it — a small but telling alignment-adjacent concern.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Missing F-35 fighter jet components last seen in Hong Kong, with Australian investigators now probing potential technology exposure — the kind of story that gets classified fast.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — ground-level view pressed flat against cracked sun-baked asphalt looking steeply upward at the underside of a massive rusted petroleum tanker truck, its belly filling the upper frame, wheels taller than a person, the vehicle completely motionless and abandoned at a fuel depot — dark crimson and charcoal palette, firelight reflections dancing across the truck's corroded undercarriage from somewhere off-screen to the left — we are in a Gulf port city, the concrete loading dock stretching away behind the truck's axles, fuel hoses hanging limp and disconnected like dead vines, a row of identical tankers queued behind this one, all stopped, none moving — the sky visible in the narrow gap between truck belly and tarmac is the color of a bruise, amber-rust haze swallowing the horizon — to the right a corrugated metal pump station sits dark and powerless, its digital price display dead and blank — heat shimmer rises off the black asphalt in visible waves — a single rusted chain-link gate in the far distance is padlocked shut, a hand-lettered paper notice fluttering against it, unreadable — the geometry of stalled commerce, of supply lines gone silent, towers above the viewer, oppressive and total.

dawn.blurb: SCIENCE GROWS BACK WHAT STROKES TOOK AWAY
dawn.summary: In a week shadowed by AI-triggered near-wars and UN war crime allegations, a quieter revolution is happening in the lab: scientists have used stem cells to regenerate stroke-damaged brain tissue in mice, growing new neurons and restoring movement that was lost. This follows recent breakthroughs in brain organoids and aging reversal — a genuine pattern of momentum in neuroscience, not a one-off. The brain, long considered irreparable, is becoming medicine's next frontier.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Stem cell therapy regenerated neurons and restored motor function after stroke in mice, a result that points toward human trials with real urgency.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi, who once disguised herself as a man to train under Taliban rule, won an Asian Games silver medal — a stunning arc of defiance and triumph.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Iran reportedly signaled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 7 days if military pressure eases, suggesting back-channel diplomacy is alive even amid open conflict.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Researchers have developed a new concrete formula that is both stronger than standard mix and actively absorbs CO2 from the atmosphere, offering a rare win-win for construction and climate.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Scientists discovered the first new penguin species in over 100 years, a reminder that Earth still holds secrets and that curiosity-driven research keeps delivering wonder.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Interior scene, we are inside a darkened neuroscience lab in the early morning hours after the breakthrough results were confirmed, looking outward through a wide floor-to-ceiling glass window toward a sunlit courtyard beyond, rich gold morning light pouring through in saturated emerald and amber shafts across the lab floor. The aftermath of a long night of discovery: a microsurgery bench sits quietly to one side, a single glass microsyringe resting in its tray, work complete. On a light table near the window, a glass slide holding a stained brain tissue cross-section glows in warm amber and deep violet, the regenerated zone visible as a soft bloom of orange and red against the stroke-darkened tissue. A monitor beside it still displays a color-coded gait analysis footprint trail, the final mouse walking pattern rendered in vivid emerald green — steady, rhythmic, restored — glowing softly in the dim room. A small transparent observation arena sits on a platform near the window, empty now, catching a warm shaft of gold morning sun. Culture flasks with faint pearlescent fluid catch the light on a nearby shelf. The courtyard beyond the window is alive with saturated green leaves backlit by afternoon-gold morning sun, vibrant and alive, the world outside luminous with emerald and gold, framed by the cool steel-blue stillness of the empty lab interior.
